brief: GS says widening European sovereign spreads, especially OAT-Bund, are starting to cap the selloff. The resulting tightening in financial conditions should limit further yield rises, so GS leans toward lower Bund and Treasury yields. That same impulse backs GS's call for one more Fed and ECB hike each, in December. GS expects Euro weakness from wider spreads to fade, with some recent losses recovered in coming weeks. Despite the yield pressure, GS says resilient earnings have pushed US equities to record highs. Consensus sees 27% y/y S&P 500 EPS growth for 3Q26, the highest going into a reporting season since 2021, and GS expects most companies to beat. European earnings have also stayed resilient even as higher rates start to bite. On Brazil, GS expects an October 25 runoff after Flávio Bolsonaro's stronger than expected first round, and says a market friendly, fiscally tighter outcome could push USD/BRL down to 4.50-4.80. GS says AI investment and enterprise adoption keep rising (23.8% in September, up from 22.4% in August), with spillovers into Europe continuing through 2027. GS expects China's export boom to keep running for a few years but says it increasingly depends on foreign markets absorbing the added Chinese supply.
